content.user_title: Build Telegram Bots with Guided Architecture
content.value_statement: Telegram bot projects need clear architecture, interaction design, and reliable API patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through bot setup, keyboards, payments, limits, and launch planning.
actual_capabilities: Compares Telegram bot stack options across Node.js and Python libraries.
Provides a basic Telegraf setup with command, text, launch, and shutdown handlers.
Shows inline keyboard menus, callback handling, and pagination patterns.
Outlines monetization models and Telegram payment invoice handling.
Covers usage limits, onboarding, error handling, and anti-spam practices.
limitations: Provides guidance and snippets, not a complete production bot.
Does not include deployment automation, database schemas, or hosting configuration.
Token handling and payment setup still require user-supplied credentials.
Examples focus on Telegraf and may need adaptation for other libraries.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Support Bot
use_cases.description: Plan commands, menus, and onboarding for a customer support bot before implementation.

use_cases.title: Design Paid Bot Features
use_cases.description: Compare freemium, subscription, and per-use models for a Telegram bot business.

use_cases.title: Standardize Bot Structure
use_cases.description: Create a maintainable project layout with handlers, services, middleware, and keyboards.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Bot Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-bot-builder to plan a Telegram bot for [audience]. Include core commands, onboarding, and one simple interaction flow.

prompt_templates.title: Design Interactive Menus
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-bot-builder to design inline keyboard flows for [bot goal]. Include menu labels, callback actions, and pagination needs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Payments and Limits
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-bot-builder to design a paid plan for [bot idea]. Compare pricing models, payment flow, usage limits, and upgrade prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telegram-bot-builder to review my planned Telegram bot architecture. Check reliability, error handling, rate limits, onboarding, and scaling risks.

output_examples.input: Create a Telegram bot plan for appointment reminders.
output: Recommended commands include start, help, add reminder, list reminders, and settings.
The onboarding flow should collect timezone, reminder preference, and notification consent.
Use inline buttons for reminder confirmation, snooze choices, and cancellation.

output_examples.input: Design a paid premium flow for a language learning bot.
output: Offer a free tier with daily practice limits and a premium tier with unlimited sessions.
Use Telegram Payments for upgrades and confirm activation after successful payment.
Show upgrade prompts only when the user reaches a clear feature limit.

output_examples.input: Review my bot for common launch risks.
output: Move slow tasks out of message handlers so Telegram responses stay fast.
Add global error handling and friendly fallback messages.
Add notification controls to reduce spam reports and user blocks.

best_practices: Store bot tokens and payment credentials in environment variables.
Acknowledge user actions quickly and move long work to background jobs.
Add global error handling, rate limits, and clear notification controls.
anti_patterns: Sending frequent unsolicited messages to users.
Blocking Telegram webhook or polling handlers with slow work.
Using complex inline keyboards without clear navigation or recovery paths.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete bot automatically?
faq.answer: It provides architecture guidance, patterns, and implementation prompts. You still need to build, test, and deploy the bot.

faq.question: Which Telegram libraries does it cover?
faq.answer: It discusses Telegraf, grammY, python-telegram-bot, and aiogram, with examples focused on Telegraf.

faq.question: Can it help with Telegram Payments?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines invoice handling, provider token usage, successful payment handling, and premium activation planning.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include deployment or hosting setup?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on bot design and code patterns, not infrastructure provisioning or deployment automation.

faq.question: How should bot secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables for bot tokens and payment credentials. Never commit real token values to source control.
